The issue is clear. In `contribute_to_class`, the `setattr` unconditionally sets `get_%s_display` on the class, which overrides any user-defined method. The fix should check if the method is already defined on the class (by the user) before setting it.

Looking at the code:
```python
if self.choices is not None:
    setattr(cls, 'get_%s_display' % self.name,
            partialmethod(cls._get_FIELD_display, field=self))
```

This always overwrites any existing method. We need to check if the user has already defined a `get_FOO_display` method on the class itself (not inherited from the base Model class).


So the solution is to inspect the class's own `__dict__` to see if the method already exists there before applying the setattr.

Now I understand the issue. In `contribute_to_class`, the `setattr` unconditionally overwrites `get_FOO_display`, even if the user defined their own. The fix is to check if the user has already defined this method on the class before overwriting it.
